summary: During the ASEAN-EU Ministerial Meeting in Brunei, Thailand informed Cambodia of its intent to withdraw from the 2001 MOU regarding overlapping maritime claims. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow argued the 20-year-old pact failed to produce progress and stated Thailand would prefer to use UNCLOS principles for future negotiations.
title: This Week in Peace: Thailand to Terminate MOU for Maritime Cooperation with Cambodia

summary: Cambodian authorities repatriated 635 Thai nationals through the Poipet-Aranyaprathet border crossing following a raid on a 13-story building housing scam operations. Thai police identified 68 individuals with online complaints and two with active arrest warrants. Officials estimate nearly 10,000 Thais remain involved in such operations across the border.
title: Cambodia pushes back 635 Thais after Poipet scam raid

summary: On May 1, Thai reporting said the government was preparing a proposal to cancel the 2001 MOU 44 maritime framework and planned to present it to Cabinet on May 5. Officials were also preparing for notification to Cambodia and a shift toward an UNCLOS-based framework; the Cabinet had not yet approved cancellation.
title: Thai government to inform Cambodia of intent to scrap 2001 Maritime MoU

summary: On May 2, Bangkok Post reported Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow saying that the Philippines, as ASEAN chair, had offered to facilitate dialogue between Thailand and Cambodia. He said a trilateral meeting could be held around the upcoming ASEAN summit in Cebu, while Thailand wanted future maritime negotiations to use an international-law framework including UNCLOS and called for restraint in public statements. The meeting was still prospective at this stage.
title: Manila offers to mediate Thai-Cambodia talks

summary: A popular social media page focusing on border maps raised concerns regarding the construction of a fence along the Thai-Cambodian border near Sisaket. The report claims the Thai military is strictly monitoring the area but keeping the project quiet to avoid Cambodian pressure, despite border markers 52-54 supposedly being settled.
title: Famous page asks why Thailand is hesitant to announce border fence construction

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn announced that Cambodia will use international law and peaceful mechanisms to handle maritime disputes if Thailand unilaterally cancels the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). He stated that the MoU is currently the only shared framework for managing overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand and its removal would force Cambodia to explore other legal avenues to protect its sovereignty.
title: Cambodia to seek legal solutions if Thailand exits maritime pact

summary: Thai authorities at the Khlong Luek border checkpoint repatriated 55 Cambodian migrant workers (34 men, 19 women, and 2 boys) after their legal cases were finalized. The operation involved coordination between the Burapha Task Force, border patrol, immigration, and health officials to ensure a structured return process.
title: Thailand repatriates 55 Cambodian workers via border

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is reportedly moving toward revoking the 2001 maritime MoU with Cambodia. Officials argue that since Cambodia joined the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) in February 2026, a 'new legal reality' exists. Thailand intends to shift away from bilateral negotiations toward this international legal framework to resolve the long-standing deadlock over the 26,000-square-kilometer Overlapping Claims Area.
title: Thailand eyes UN maritime law to resolve Cambodia border dispute

summary: The Thai government is strengthening cooperation with the US to dismantle major call center networks and human trafficking rings operating along the Thai-Cambodian border. Recent operations discovered over 10,000 victims of forced labor and romance scams of various nationalities. The Prime Minister emphasized that Thailand will not be a transit point for these criminal organizations and aims to reach Tier 1 status in the TIP report.
title: Thailand-US Expand Cooperation to Combat Scammers and Human Trafficking Near Borders

summary: The Thaiger reported that all 635 Thai nationals were repatriated from Cambodia on April 30 in two batches: 350 at about 16:50 and the remaining 285 at about 18:20. Thai officials screened the returnees to distinguish potential victims from people suspected of knowingly participating in criminal activity.
title: Cambodia scam crackdown sends 635 Thais back home

summary: Cambodian analysts and officials have reacted strongly to statements made by Thailand's UN representative regarding historical aid provided to Cambodia. While Thailand claims its past support justifies current border security measures, Cambodian experts call this a distortion of history. They allege that Thai blockades have displaced thousands of Cambodian households and claim that Thailand is using the narrative of 'gratitude' to mask violations of sovereignty. Tensions remain high as both sides exchange accusations of initiating armed attacks last year.
title: Experts reject Thai claims of past aid to justify actions against Cambodia

summary: The Burapha Task Force, in coordination with Aranyaprathet immigration and customs, processed the repatriation of 55 Cambodian nationals (34 men, 19 women, and 2 children) at the Ban Khlong Luek Permanent Border Checkpoint in Sa Kaeo. These individuals had completed their legal sentences for various offenses. Thai authorities handed them over to Cambodian officials at the Thai-Cambodian Friendship Bridge. Security remains tight along the border to maintain stability according to army policy.
title: Thai Burapha Task Force Pushes 55 Cambodians Back Across Border After Legal Cases End

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen warned that Thailand's push to cancel the 2001 maritime MoU (MOU 44) could dismantle the long-standing bilateral framework for managing overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. Citing Thai security experts, he suggested the move is driven by nationalism and questioned if it is an attempt to 'internationalize' the dispute. He expressed respect for Thai analysts who oppose the cancellation and warned that moving away from bilateral talks could complicate future negotiations.
title: Hun Sen warns Thai move to end maritime MoU may fuel row

summary: Khmer Times reported a CMAC assessment published May 4 in which Director-General Heng Ratana said about 85% of prioritized residential areas had been cleared while farmland and border areas remained heavily contaminated. Ratana said some previously cleared locations had become newly affected by cluster munitions and that disputed-area contamination was complicating Cambodia's 2030 mine-free goal. The article also relayed Cambodian mine-action authorities' attribution of some recent cluster-munition contamination and casualties to Thailand.
title: 85% of homes cleared, but farmland still at risk of blasts

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow announced that Thailand is awaiting a response from Cambodia regarding a proposed trilateral meeting including the Philippines. The talks are intended to take place on the sidelines of the 48th ASEAN Summit in the Philippines from May 7 to 9, 2026. The meeting aims to address regional stability and the ongoing bilateral tensions.
title: Thai Foreign Minister expects Cambodia to join trilateral talks at ASEAN summit

summary: Reporting on the statements from Cambodian officials, Thai media highlights the growing friction over the maritime dispute. Kung Phoak stated that the MoU 44 was intended to resolve overlapping claims through joint development while respecting sovereignty, but lamented that the mechanism has barely been utilized. With Thailand moving toward cancellation, the focus shifts to UNCLOS as the new arena for mediation. This follows earlier positions from Thai officials who suggested a similar shift toward international standards if bilateral talks fail.
title: Cambodian Minister Disappointed as Thailand Set to Cancel MOU 44; Both Nations to Deal via UNCLOS

summary: The Thai Cabinet approved the cancellation of the 2001 maritime agreement with Cambodia to align future negotiations with UNCLOS. Thai officials cited the need to update the framework after two decades without tangible results. Thailand plans to establish technical and legal committees to manage the new framework while maintaining that it remains committed to international law.
title: Thailand scraps maritime agreement with Cambodia, turns to UN framework

summary: On May 5, Reuters reported that Thailand's Cabinet approved cancellation of the 2001 MOU 44 maritime framework after roughly 25 years without agreement. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul described the move as an election commitment; Cambodia's Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret and said Cambodia would pursue compulsory conciliation under UNCLOS.
title: Thailand scraps 25-year-old agreement with Cambodia on joint energy exploration

summary: Cambodian Secretary of State Kung Phoak stated that Cambodia is prepared to invoke international legal mechanisms under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) if Thailand unilaterally withdraws from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). This move signals a shift from bilateral talks to international mediation. Thailand's Cabinet is reportedly expected to meet today to consider the proposal to withdraw from the MoU, which has governed overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand for 25 years.
title: Cambodia signals UNCLOS route if Thailand scraps maritime MoU

summary: Following two rounds of armed conflict last year that killed nearly 150 people, the Thai government has formally cancelled MOU 44. PM Anutin, who campaigned on a nationalist platform, stated that the 2001 pact failed to yield results. In response, Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret and announced that Cambodia will initiate a compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS. Although a ceasefire has been in place since late December 2025, Thai officials confirmed that border checkpoints will remain closed until Cambodia fully complies with the joint ceasefire terms.
title: Thailand scraps sea boundary pact with Cambodia

summary: On May 5, Cambodia announced that it would pursue compulsory conciliation under UNCLOS after Thailand's Cabinet approved cancellation of the 2001 maritime MOU. Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn described the MOU as the only bilateral framework for the dispute and expressed deep regret over Thailand's decision.
title: Sea you in court: Cambodia announces UNCLOS conciliation as Thais exit maritime MoU

summary: Banteay Meanchey provincial officials and government spokesperson Pen Bona reported that Cambodia has completed nearly 3,000 temporary housing units in Banteay Meanchey, with work underway on about 600 units in Preah Vihear and more than 200 in Oddar Meanchey for displaced border residents. Deputy provincial governor Khlok Nuoy stated that 2,805 families are living in temporary shelters in Svay Chek district following the closure of emergency camps, while agricultural aid and plots of land are being allocated to affected households.

Anutin assured that security forces are maintaining strict vigilance along the border, but the situation remains stable.
title: PM Anutin says Cabinet axes MOU 44, confident it won't impact border

While the conciliation outcome is non-binding, it signals Cambodia's move to take the dispute to an international level.

The government intends to use the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to ensure a more systematic and international approach to the dispute. Thailand has informally notified Cambodia and is preparing a formal letter to follow.
title: Government Emphasizes Cancelling 1994 MOU Is Not Ending Negotiations, Uses UNCLOS Framework to Enhance National Interest Protection

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the Thai Cabinet has officially voted to terminate the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. He reassured the public that the military remains on high alert and that the cancellation should not increase border tensions, noting that security forces report a stabilizing situation.
title: PM Anutin reveals Cabinet resolution to cancel MOU 44, confident it won't affect border

The government is preparing to formally notify Cambodia and will establish new technical and legal committees to handle the transition under the new international law framework.
title: Government shifts to international law for maritime dispute after ending MOU 44

Both leaders agreed to have their foreign ministers develop 'practical, confidence-building measures' to normalize relations following the deadly border clashes of late 2025.

PM Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to peaceful legal solutions, while PM Anutin acknowledged that war only brings loss. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) mandate was extended until July to monitor the border.

title: Cambodia briefs diplomats on Thailand's scrapping of maritime MOU

Foreign ministers from both nations will implement 'confidence-building measures' immediately, focusing on shared interests to maintain the current uneasy truce.

title: Thailand acknowledged Cambodia's notification to proceed with the compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS

The leaders focused on maintaining a 'positive atmosphere' and using existing JBC and GBC frameworks to manage the relationship while military deployments remain in place.

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) clarified a viral report about Cambodian soldiers encroaching on Thai territory in Buriram province. Investigations confirmed they were local Thai citizens who regularly speak Khmer in daily life. No gunshots were fired as rumored. The Army urged the public to verify information before sharing to avoid panic.
title: Army Clarifies: Misunderstanding Over Cambodian Incursion in Buriram; Actually Thai Citizens Speaking Khmer

summary: Thai anti-human trafficking police arrested 4 suspects in a major transnational crime network that lured Thai citizens to Cambodia. Victims were taken through Sa Kaeo province and forced to work for scam centers, specifically for facial scanning to bypass bank security for 'mule accounts' used in money laundering. The gang reportedly has over 40 members and targets Thais looking for work, transporting them to the border where Cambodian partners pick them up.
title: Human Trafficking Network Busted: Thais Lured to Cambodia for Facial Scanning Scams

He said Cambodia would instead pursue compulsory conciliation under UNCLOS, arguing that Thailand could not discard the bilateral framework and then ask to restart bilateral talks on new terms.
title: Cambodia to pursue UN legal mechanism, rejecting bilateral talks with Thailand over maritime dispute: PM

title: Fears grow over Koh Kut sovereignty

summary: On May 13, Cambodia's Culture Ministry rejected Thailand's registration of Tamone, Ta Krabei and K'nar temples as Thai national monuments. The ministry called the registration illegal, null and without legal effect, and said a unilateral domestic listing could not establish sovereignty or delimit the international border. The report establishes Cambodia's protest and legal position, not the underlying sovereignty claim.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of registering occupied temples to bolster border claims

summary: An in-depth commentary published by Fresh News sharply criticized Thailand's Fine Arts Department for registering the Ta Moan temple complex, Ta Krabey Temple, and K'nar Temple as Thai ancient monuments. The piece asserts that domestic registration cannot create sovereignty or override international border treaties like the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1907 and the MoU 2000. It accuses Thailand of trying to build an 'artificial legitimacy' over Cambodian cultural sites along the border and destabilizing the framework of international border order.
title: Thailand Is Using Khmer Heritage to Create “Artificial Legitimacy”: Is This the Conduct of a Civilized Nation?

summary: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Military and State Security, Somboon Noonnual, stated that the situation along the Thailand-Cambodia border is currently normal and peaceful. He addressed reports of gunfire from the Cambodian side, characterizing it as an attempt by Cambodia to create a narrative and spin nationalist sentiments, emphasizing that the firing took place strictly within Cambodian territory and did not cross into Thailand. He acknowledged that Thailand's recent cancellation of MOU 44 played a role in inducing Cambodia to adhere more strictly to international frameworks, while confirming that the Thai military remains patient and prepared, including plans to construct border fences in appropriate locations.
title: Senate Military Committee Chairman insists Thailand-Cambodia border remains peaceful, dismisses Cambodian gunfire as 'image-making'

summary: The Thai Navy Chief of Staff confirmed that the situation along the eastern border with Cambodia, specifically in Chanthaburi and Trat provinces, remains under control with no provocations reported.
title: Navy Chief of Staff confirms border situation in Trat and Chanthaburi is normal and under control

summary: Admiral Thadawut Thadpithakkul, Chief of Staff of the Royal Thai Navy, stated that the border situation between Thailand and Cambodia adjacent to Trat province remains completely normal. The Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defense Command has full control over the situation, and there have been no provocations from the other side.
title: Navy chief of staff confirms eastern Thailand-Cambodia border normal, 100% under control

summary: Cambodian state media analyzed the aftermath of Thailand's unilateral termination of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44). Cambodia maintains that international legal processes and structured arbitration should now take over, criticizing Thailand's sudden flip-flop on negotiation mechanisms.
title: Thailand Destroyed the Bilateral Framework—Now Let International Law Work

The two Thais admitted to working as administrators for an online gambling operation but fled after Cambodian authorities launched heavy crackdowns on scam networks.
title: 17 illegal border-crossers arrested in Chanthaburi

Cambodia maintains that K'nar Temple, alongside Tamone Thom and Ta Krabey, is located entirely within its sovereign territory according to the 1904 and 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaties. The ministry characterized Thailand's actions as an unlawful attempt to create a 'fait accompli' on the ground to back up its occupation by force, declaring these activities null, void, and without legal effect under international law.
title: Cambodia Condemns Thailand's Activities at K'nar Temple as Sovereignty Violation

title: Thailand Provokes New Military Activities After Revoking the 2001 MOU

The committee suggests that recent ceasefire agreements and new border control mechanisms should serve as the new reference point for future relations, as the current framework has failed to prevent tensions.
title: Senate panel urges scrapping of MOU43, citing legal flaws and disputed maps

Following the discussion, Cambodian authorities agreed to have the villagers stop their farming activities until the formal border line is officially clarified.
title: Thai rangers halt Cambodian farming activity in Sa Kaeo border area

Thai rangers held discussions with Cambodian military personnel on the ground. Both sides reached an initial agreement for the Cambodian villagers to halt all land preparation activities until the territorial boundary line in the area is officially surveyed and clarified by border demarcation officials.
title: Thai rangers halt Cambodian farming activity in Sa Kaeo border area

summary: The Thai Senate reviewed a study conducted by an extraordinary committee led by Senator Noppadol Inna regarding the pros and cons of cancelling the 2000 and 2001 MOUs (MOU 43 and MOU 44). The committee unanimously proposed that the government revoke MOU 43, following the previous cabinet decision on May 5 to scrap MOU 44, citing constitutional compliance issues and 26 years of stagnant border demarcation. However, minority senators, including Pornchai Wityalertpan, strongly opposed the move, warning that canceling it without strong justification could allow corporate groups to seize overlapping maritime energy interests and leave Thailand at a disadvantage.
title: Senate committee urges government to scrap MOU 43; minority senators fear Thailand could lose advantage to Cambodia

The underlying shooting claim is disputed and this article is not independent corroboration of the Thai Army account.

title: Thailand refutes Cambodia’s claim of firing shots at border
summary: Thai Newsroom reported the Second Army Region’s May 24 denial that Thai troops fired 22 rounds at Chong Chom/O’Smach. The Thai side said no firearms were used, that Cambodian soldiers moved closer to the barbed-wire line at about 09:24, and that Thai troops issued verbal warnings and warning signals as area-control measures. The report also states Cambodia’s allegation of 12 shots from 09:24–09:45 and another 10 at 10:10.

title: Thai Navy Intercepts Seven Thais Attempting to Cross Into Cambodia
summary: Thai Tabloid reported that at 06:00 on May 24, Thai naval border forces detained seven Thai nationals with luggage near Ban Marum in Chanthaburi while they were preparing to cross into Cambodia through a natural route.

title: Cambodian Defence Ministry Rejects Thai Media Claims of Gunfire at O’Smach Border Checkpoint
summary: AKP reproduced a May 13 Cambodian Defence Ministry statement categorically denying reports that Cambodian forces fired 11 rounds at the O'Smach International Border Checkpoint. Ministry spokeswoman Lt Gen Maly Socheata called the allegation false and a serious distortion of the facts and reiterated Cambodia's commitment to border stability and peaceful mechanisms.

title: Thai Army on alert after shots fired from Cambodian side of Surin border
summary: Thai PBS World reported Royal Thai Army spokesman Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree's account that Thai troops heard 11 small-arms shots from the Cambodian side near O'Smach at about 18:40 on May 13. Thailand did not return fire and assessed the shots as scattered rather than tactically directed. The same report included Cambodia's denial that its forces fired the rounds.
